Subject: Post-call: On-prem / air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops questions

Hi Paul  thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

Summary:
- Customer preference: private, on-prem air-gapped deployment (VPC + physical airgap layer) for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Primary concerns: hardware refresh cycles, OS/firmware upgrade strategy, offline operational procedures, and remote emergency support.

Open questions we promised to follow up on (see attachments):
1) Hardware footprint: do you have existing preferred vendor/part numbers for servers and NVMe layout? We want to confirm GPU model (A100, H100, etc.), NICs, and minimum RAM per node.
2) Maintenance windows & upgrades: how do you typically handle BIOS/firmware/OS upgrades in air-gapped environments? Are you open to scheduled full-cluster maintenance windows or do you require rolling upgrades only?
3) Offline ops & monitoring: what's your plan for telemetry and alerting for an air-gapped cluster? Do you have an internal SAT/console for local monitoring or will you need our on-prem agent to run without internet egress?
4) Emergency support & access: in escalations, are you willing to provide temporary supervised access or do we need to restrict support to runbooks and on-site engineers only?

Next steps: 
- Paul to confirm answers above and share any hardware spec docs.
- Neha to follow up with an on-prem/airgap checklist and offline ops runbook (I attached a draft).
- Michael to share procurement / PO timeline and T&Cs for Dedicated vs Private pricing options.

Attaching: redwood_onprem_airgap_checklist.pdf (draft), hardware_spec_sheet.xlsx (template), offline_ops_runbook.docx (sample).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min SRE call next week to walk the ops team through the checklist.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: On-prem / air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops questions

Marissa  thanks for the notes and the checklist. A few quick answers to get the ball rolling: 

1) Hardware: we are standardizing on H100 nodes for inference, typically 8x H100 per chassis right now. Preferred vendors are Dell R760xa and Supermicro AS - I can share exact SKUs early next week. NVMe layout is 4 x 3.84TB per node. Memory target is 1.5TB/node for our largest models.
2) Upgrades: in our air-gapped DCs we prefer quarterly rolling upgrades with maintenance windows. We do not permit full-cluster reboot windows unless coordinated 8+ weeks in advance. BIOS/firmware is handled by our server ops team and we apply signed bundles staged via an internal update station.
3) Monitoring: we run a local Prometheus + Grafana stack with push-gateway for metrics; no outbound telemetry allowed. We will need Redwood's on-prem agent to operate entirely offline and write to local sinks (Prometheus).
4) Emergency support: we do not permit remote vendor shell access. For high-severity incidents we can provide supervised on-site access or host a remote session with a named SRE and audited keystroke logging.

I'll attach our internal hardware SKU list and internal ops constraints after I get permission from procurement (should have it by Mon 12/20). Happy to have the SRE call  Tue 12/21 looks good.

 Paul

Hi Paul / Marissa  attaching a more detailed checklist and a short offline ops runbook. Key highlights included in the doc: 

- Hardware prechecks: GPU firmware parity, NVMe SMART verification, BIOS settings to enable SR-IOV and IOMMU for NICs, recommended kernel parameters for low-latency inference. 
- Image/upgrade workflow: support for signed update bundles delivered via USB staging or internal update station; checksum verification steps; rollback plan and snapshot cadence. 
- Monitoring & logging: instructions to configure the Redwood agent to write Prometheus metrics locally and rotate logs to the bank's centralized file system. 
- Emergency playbook: supervised on-site access flow, contact matrix, required audit artifacts (timestamps, operator identity, keystroke logging if available).

Attachments: redwood_onprem_airgap_checklist.pdf (updated), offline_ops_runbook.docx (detailed), hardware_spec_sheet.xlsx (compatibility table).
